# Introduction {.unnumbered}

Welcome to the Quarto version of the Reed thesis template. If you've never used Quarto
or Markdown before, you'll have a short learning period, but the payoff is a document that
is consistent, easy to keep under version control, and that can produce both a
Reed-formatted **PDF** (through the `reedthesis` LaTeX class) and a Reed-formatted
**Word** document (through the Reed Word template) from the same source files.

Quarto lets you mix your writing with **R** or **Python** code. The code runs when you
render the thesis, so your figures, tables and numbers always match your analysis.

This introduction is unnumbered on purpose: the first numbered chapter comes next. To
add another unnumbered chapter, put `{.unnumbered}` after its title, as in the first line
of this file.

## Why use it?

Quarto does a great job of keeping your text separate from how it looks. Change the
bibliography style, the spacing, or the output format in one place (`_quarto.yml`) and the
whole thesis follows. Under the hood, the PDF is typeset by LaTeX, which has an excellent
line-breaking algorithm, automatic ligatures, and is the best way to typeset good-looking
mathematics.

## Who should use it?

Anyone who wants reproducible analysis in their thesis, needs math, tables, many figures,
cross-references or citations, or just cares about the final appearance of their document.
At Reed, math majors are required to use LaTeX and many science majors will want to; this
template lets you write in Markdown and still get the same Reed class file.

## Rendering your thesis

From this folder, run one of:

```bash
quarto render --to pdf      # PDF using reedthesis.cls
quarto render --to docx     # Word using the Reed Word template
quarto render               # both
```

The output is written to `_book/`. Your title, name, advisor, division, department and
front matter (acknowledgments, preface, abstract, dedication, abbreviations) all live in
`_quarto.yml`.
